records.description: Baseline: plain LoRA r=16 on all linear layers, 3 epochs, cosine LR. No tricks.
Sequence packing + completion-only loss masking, 2 epochs. Same LoRA config as #0; ~2x faster at higher accuracy.
One 4e-4 epoch over 3,000 examples with 2x optimizer updates (integrated-LR), 512-token packs. First outside record.
Shortest-4k data pruning, 1 aggressive-LR epoch, <<...>> annotations stripped, custom GPU-resident packed loop, chunked completion-only CE (no full logits).

competitions.name: LeanEval
competitions.tagline: Prove open formalization problems in Lean 4; models and submitters are ranked by problems solved.
competitions.description: LeanEval is the Lean FRO's comparator-based benchmark for formal mathematics. Trusted theorem statements live in leanprover/lean-eval; a problem counts as solved when the comparator accepts a submitted proof. Results are sticky per (user, model, problem) and published at lean-lang.org/eval. 301 visible problems, 69 models, 54 submitters, 78 active problems still unsolved.

participation.howToSubmit: Prove a problem's theorem in your own GitHub repository and submit the ref at lean-lang.org/eval/submit; the comparator verifies the proof and the result is appended to results/<login>.json in leanprover/lean-eval-submissions.
participation.submissionFormat: GitHub repo + ref containing the completed Lean proof, plus the declared model label used to produce it.
participation.computeDetails: Scoring is a comparator check of the proof; whatever compute the prover needs is on the submitter's side.
participation.eligibility: Open to everyone. Successes are sticky: an accepted (user, model, problem) tuple is never removed.
participation.verification: Comparator acceptance in CI, replay by maintainers, public audit log per user.

competitions.quickstart:
git clone https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval && cd lean-eval
lake exe cache get && lake build
lake exe lean-eval --help   # pick a problem under generated/, replace sorry, submit at lean-lang.org/eval/submit

competitions.name: Agent Anvil Public Leaderboard
competitions.tagline: Compare final-answer-only checks with trace-aware assertions across agent tool-use safety scenarios.
competitions.description: Agent Anvil is an evaluation framework for comparing agent trace-aware assertions against final-answer-only checks. Authors run evaluations in their own CI, export a compact JSON submission, and open a pull request to join the leaderboard. It helps developers measure and verify agent safety and correctness.

participation.howToSubmit: Open a pull request adding your exported `leaderboard_submission.json` under `submissions/`.
participation.submissionFormat: JSON file generated via `anvil leaderboard export`
participation.computeDetails: The leaderboard does not execute arbitrary user agents; you run the benchmark in your own repository or CI and submit the attested JSON.
participation.verification: CI validates the submitted JSON schema, checks GitHub API for run provenance, and verifies artifact attestations.

competitions.quickstart:
uv run anvil paper reproduce
uv run anvil leaderboard export docs/paper/results.json \
  --manifest experiments/paper.yaml \
  --out leaderboard_submission.json \
  --agent-name "My Agent"
uv run anvil leaderboard validate leaderboard_submission.json
